Table 7-10  Key Recommendations to Decrease Gas and Bloating
Certain foods can produce excess gas during digestion and may worsen your symptoms of abdominal pain or 
bloating. Various foods affect people in different ways; avoid these foods if they cause you discomfort. The 
following diet tips may improve your symptoms.
Foods that may cause gas:
•	 Beans, cabbage, cauliflower, brussel sprouts, broccoli, asparagus, peppers, cucumbers, onions, garlic, radishes, 
sauerkraut
•	 Raw apples, avocado, melon
•	 Eggs, fried and fatty foods, spicy foods, carbonated beverages
Swallowing air may also cause excess gas. To prevent this:
•	 Eat slowly
•	 Avoid chewing gum, drinking carbonated beverages, and smoking

Diverticulitis
Diverticulitis occurs when there is inflammation or perforation at the site of a diverticuli. Manage­
ment focuses on resolution of inflammation. Bowel rest is often indicated with gradual diet 
advancement. As eating resumes, patients should maintain a low-fiber intake until the inflamma­
tion is resolved. The diet should be advanced slowly as tolerance permits, and fiber intake should 
be gradually increased. Eventual return to a high-fiber diet should be encouraged, as well as con­
sumption of adequate fluids.
